cat > index.qmd << 'QMDEOF'
---
title: "Juan Franco"
jupyter: python3
---

Hi, I'm Juan Franco. I'm a Senior Data Analyst at Royal Caribbean Group, and I'm
completing a master's degree in Business Analytics at Boston University. This
site is my course ePortfolio for AD688, Big Data and Cloud Analytics for
Business.

<p style="text-align: center;"><img src="images/data-center.jpg" alt="A data center interior" style="width: 75%;"></p>

## Environment check

The cell below runs PySpark directly on the AWS EC2 instance used throughout
this course, and lists my coursework in the Business Analytics program. METAD
688 is the course I am currently completing.

```{python}
#| include: false
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

spark = (
    SparkSession.builder
    .appName("PortfolioDemo")
    .master("local[*]")
    .config("spark.ui.showConsoleProgress", "false")
    .getOrCreate()
)
spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("ERROR")
```

```{python}
courses = spark.createDataFrame(
    [
        ("METAD 605",  "Operations Management"),
        ("METAD 571S", "Business Analytics Foundations"),
        ("METAD 616S", "Enterprise Risk Analytics"),
        ("METAD 715S", "Quantitative and Qualitative Decision Making"),
        ("METAD 599",  "Python and SQL for Business Analytics"),
        ("METAD 699",  "Data Mining for Business Analytics"),
        ("METAD 632S", "Financial Concepts"),
        ("METAD 688",  "Big Data and Cloud Analytics for Business"),
    ],
    ["course_code", "course_title"],
)

courses.show(truncate=False)
spark.stop()
QMDEOF
```

The quoted `'QMDEOF'` means bash writes everything literally — no substitutions, backticks intact.

**One thing that needs your hand:** the heredoc can't carry the final closing fence, because three backticks alone on a line would end my code block here. So after running that, open `index.qmd` in the editor and add a line at the very end containing three backticks. Then verify:

```bash
grep -c '```' index.qmd
```
